No company-specific news; it trades with the broader AI complex as investors hunt winners beyond Nvidia.
Beat earnings with strong guidance, but the CEO resignation scandal, a congressional report on China's military seeking its chips, and a probe into Lutnick/Cantor keep headline risk high.

Internal documents on pushing teens into Instagram add to its regulatory and reputational risk.
No hard news; commentary pieces debate whether its 2027 story justifies the stock's weak year.

top_buys.pitch: Outage-driven panic buying plus a defensive rotation lands in Costco's lap.
top_buys.why: Reporting says shoppers hit by repeated tech and banking outages are stocking up on emergency goods, and Costco is seeing the spending. Staples is the only sector with a positive week while technology is down nearly 6%, so flows favor it. Costco also reports monthly sales, which gives the story a chance to be confirmed in data rather than fade as a one-day headline.
top_buys.risks: Costco trades at a rich multiple, so even good sales news can fail to move it, and a quick resolution of the outages removes the catalyst.
top_buys.watch: Costco's next monthly comparable sales release and any new large-scale tech outage.

top_buys.company: Real Estate Select Sector SPDR Fund
top_buys.pitch: A December rate hike is the wrong backdrop for property stocks.
top_buys.why: Fed officials including Waller are publicly backing more aggressive action, and the dollar and yields jumped while gold fell to a 14-month low. Mortgage demand already dropped as rates hit a three-week high. REITs are heavily dependent on cheap financing and tend to re-rate lower over weeks as yields grind up, not just on the first headline.
top_buys.risks: A soft inflation print or dovish Fed speaker could reverse rate expectations fast, and REITs are already down 1.9% on the week.
top_buys.watch: Upcoming inflation data and Fed speakers ahead of the December meeting.

top_buys.pitch: Higher-for-longer rates are a tailwind for big-bank lending margins.
top_buys.why: The Fed looks set to hike again in December, which generally widens the spread banks earn on loans and cash balances. Analysts are already framing rate-sensitive financials like Schwab as winners from this setup, and that logic extends to the large deposit-funded banks. Financials are down 3.3% this week, so the rate benefit is not yet reflected in the price.
top_buys.risks: Higher rates also raise recession and credit-loss fears, and a broad market selloff would drag banks down regardless of margins.
top_buys.watch: December Fed decision and any early commentary on fourth-quarter net interest income.

top_buys.pitch: A guidance raise in a bad housing market shows real execution.
top_buys.why: Lowe's posted 9.3% sales growth, a sixth straight quarter of positive comps, and raised its full-year outlook on strength in pro, online and appliances. That happened despite high mortgage rates holding back housing turnover, which suggests share gains rather than a cyclical bounce. Guidance raises tend to support a stock for weeks as estimates get revised up.
top_buys.risks: The stock may already have popped on the print, and another leg up in mortgage rates could choke home-improvement demand.
top_buys.watch: Analyst estimate revisions this week and holiday-quarter traffic data.

top_buys.pitch: The same outage-driven stock-up behavior and defensive rotation help Walmart.
top_buys.why: Consumers racing to buy emergency goods after repeated tech failures spend at mass retailers, and staples is the only sector up this week. Walmart's scale and grocery mix make it a natural destination for that spending. It is also a classic rotation target when investors flee high-multiple tech.
top_buys.risks: Walmart's valuation is already full and a tech rebound would pull money back out of defensives.
top_buys.watch: Walmart's quarterly results and monthly retail sales data.
